note: English wording of emergencies.json for the English interface. Same ids, same order; emergencies.json is the source.

operator_actions: Keep track of how long the power has been off
Turn on spare aeration or emergency oxygen if you have it
Have a spare oxygen tank ready; swap it if the power is off for more than 6 hours
When the power is back: switch equipment on one by one, close the emergency oxygen, check the young eels

emergencies.trigger: Aerator off because of a power cut (ponds without the Synt Nursery system)
operator_actions: Note the time the power went out and tell the farm owner
Start the generator, or connect the aerator to a battery backup, if there is one
Do not feed until the aerator is running again
Look at the eels every 30 minutes: rising to the surface or crowding at the water inlet means oxygen is short
If the power is out for more than 1 hour with no backup, slowly let in clean water that has been settled
When the power is back: turn the aerator on first, then the other equipment one by one, and look at the eels

emergencies.trigger: Main pump failed or flow below 50%
operator_actions: Make sure the aeration keeps running
Swap the pump (keep a spare)
Check for blockages

emergencies.trigger: Pond DO below 4 mg/L, or signs of low DO (young eels rising to the surface or crowding at the inlet)
operator_actions: Check the aerator, air stones and air hoses
Turn on a spare aerator or emergency oxygen if you have one
Do not feed until the eels swim normally
Check the heater or cooler capacity and the room conditions
Give shade when it is hot
Feed less
Add zeolite
Check the biofilter

emergencies.trigger: Heavy rain, or a muddy water source after rain
operator_actions: Cover or divert rainwater so large amounts do not run into the ponds
Stop taking water from the source while it is muddy
Use water from the settling or quarantine pond you prepared
Measure pH, TDS and temperature after the rain; sudden changes stress the eels
